title: The 'Superman' Recovery (British Open)
focus: Recovery path to the T-zone after an extreme front-court lunge/dive.
prompt: Analyze the player in black (Paul Coll). Focus on his recovery path to the T-zone after the extreme lunge/dive in the front court.
key_points: Resilience: after the desperate retrieve, pushes off the floor immediately using the core and the front lunging leg.
Visual discipline: eyes stay fixed on the front wall and the opponent; the head never drops.
Efficiency: explosive crossover step; back dominating the T-zone before the opponent can strike.
Principle: never admire your own shot - the point continues until the ball bounces twice; immediate T-recovery is non-negotiable.

title: Front-Court Volley Drill (Extreme Reaction)
focus: Racket preparation, backswing length and wrist stability in rapid volleys.
prompt: Analyze the rapid front-wall volley drill. Focus on racket preparation, backswing length, and wrist stability.
key_points: Shortened backswing: virtually eliminated at this pace; the racket head stays up and in front of the body.
Locked wrist: power comes from forearm rotation and slight body weight transfer, not wrist flick.
Target fixation: excellent hand-eye coordination with zero wasted movement.
Principle: on aggressive front-court volleys, shorten the swing, lock the wrist, prepare the racket extremely early.
